messages.content:
You are verifying one structured PFAS study evidence record against the
complete source evidence cited by that record.

You receive:
1. the review task and task-specific extraction objective;
2. the held-out anchor identifiers;
3. one extracted evidence record; and
4. the complete source chunks or inspected source-page text referenced by the
   record.

Judge only source support and transcription. Do not reward usefulness,
verbosity, or agreement with general background knowledge.

Assess every substantive populated source-dependent field against only its
attached field-level locators. Do not create separate assessments for locator
arrays, record IDs, or formatting metadata:
- supported: the cited evidence directly supports the field and its material
  qualifiers;
- partially_supported: the core statement is supported but a material
  qualifier, condition, denominator, or scope is missing;
- unsupported: the cited evidence does not establish the field;
- contradicted: the cited evidence directly conflicts with the field.

For quantitative_findings, value must contain an actual number, censored or
approximate number, range, or explicit ND/not-detected result. A unit-shaped
string such as "nmol/L" in value with an empty unit is a unit error even when
the source mentions that concentration scale. Do not silently reinterpret one
schema field as another. Confirm that value matches value_form; explanatory
text and uncertainty belong in qualifiers.

Classify endpoint_type from the measured basis, not the source's terminology.
Parent-compound loss alone is not destruction; phase transfer is not
degradation; inorganic fluoride release or fluorine-balance closure establishes
defluorination but not mineralization. Mineralization requires direct
carbon-fate evidence such as measured CO2/inorganic carbon or a carbon balance.
If an author calls defluorination mineralization without that evidence, retain
the author phrase only as reported_term and mark endpoint_type=mineralization
unsupported with error_type=endpoint_classification.

Comparability is an analyst-derived judgment. Do not require the source to
state the comparability conclusion verbatim. Instead, judge whether its status
and reason follow conservatively from supported cited fields for matrix, PFAS
scope, scale, conditions, endpoint, unit, and denominator.

An author_reported limitation requires direct source support. A
design_inferred limitation is supported when it follows necessarily from
cited design facts; absence from the supplied packet is not a study
limitation.

Classify errors as numeric_transcription, unit, qualifier,
endpoint_classification, source_attribution, other, or none. A record is usable
only if its source identity, matrix, treatment, endpoints, and quantitative
findings are not unsupported or contradicted in a way that would mislead
  synthesis. A usable record can still contain non-core fields that synthesis
must exclude according to their field assessments.

For metric consistency, always emit separate assessments with these exact
field-path forms when the corresponding item exists:
- `quantitative_findings[i].value`;
- `quantitative_findings[i].unit`;
- `operating_conditions[i].value`;
- `operating_conditions[i].unit`;
- `endpoints[i].endpoint_type`; and
- `comparability.status`.

Other substantive fields may be assessed individually or as a whole object,
but do not omit these required assessment types and do not emit a required
field path more than once.

Report anchor_exclusion_violation=true if the source resolves to any held-out
anchor DOI, URL, exact title, or corpus source.

Return one JSON object that follows the supplied verification schema exactly.

field_assessments.reason: Methods text states that all AER columns were operated with 2000 BV of tap water spiked with 11 PFAS at 200 ng/L each and an EBCT of 3 min, and selectivity coefficients were calculated across AER–PFAS–anion combinations. This supports that tests share the same matrix, influent, EBCT, run length, and comparable endpoints, justifying “comparable_with_conditions.”

Fig. 5 description notes “effluent concentrations of 11 types of PFAS from AER columns” where all columns were run with PFAS‑spiked tap water, indicating evaluation of PFAS removal (phase transfer to AERs) via effluent concentrations, consistent with endpoint_type “removal.”

Fig. 4 is described as comparison of “selectivity coefficients” among anions, PFAS, and AERs, which are dimensionless ratios quantifying adsorption preference. This is not a removal fraction or capacity, so classifying as endpoint_type “other” is appropriate.

The cited methods text specifies that all columns were operated with 2000 BV of tap water spiked with 11 PFAS (200 ng/L each) at an EBCT of 3 min. The limitation statement simply interprets this fixed design (single influent concentration and EBCT over 2000 BV) as a constraint; as a design-inferred limitation it follows directly from the reported conditions.

The methods state: “All columns were operated with 2000 BV of tap water spiked with 11 types of PFAS (to a concentration of 200 ng/L each) with an EBCT of 3 min,” which directly supports “Tap water spiked with 11 PFAS at equal concentrations.”
The text states “tap water spiked with 11 types of PFAS (to a concentration of 200 ng/L each),” matching the value 200 for influent PFAS concentration for each compound.
Concentrations are explicitly given in ng/L (“200 ng/L each”), matching the recorded unit ng/L.
The methods note an “EBCT of 3 min,” matching the value 3 for empty bed contact time.
EBCT is given as “3 min,” matching the unit min.
The methods state “All columns were operated with 2000 BV of tap water…,” matching the value 2000 for bed volumes treated.
Bed volumes are expressed as “BV” in the text, matching the recorded unit BV.

The cited text provides the selectivity order among synthesized AERs: “Gel(12-1-1) > Gel(4-4-4) ≈ MP(12-1-1) > Gel(8-1-1) > MP(8-1-1) ≈ MP(4-4-4) > MP(4-4-0) > MP(8-0-0),” which matches part of the value. However, the same locator text does not mention commercial AERs or PFA694E; inclusion of “commercial AERs including PFA694E” is not supported by this locator and over-extends the statement.
This field is intentionally unitless (a list of resin structures and a qualitative order); leaving unit as null is appropriate and consistent with the text.

The methods describe comparison of selectivity coefficients among inorganic anions and explicitly mention chloride, sulfate, and nitrate, along with their relative impact; listing these as coexisting inorganic anions is supported.

The discussion/methods describe polystyrene-based AERs synthesized with different amines with long alkyl chains, strong-base quaternary amine functional groups, and note that gel-type AERs show higher selectivity than macroporous AERs. This supports the description of functional groups, varying alkyl chain lengths/symmetry, and gel vs macroporous structures.
PFBA is explicitly mentioned in the RSSCT results (“PFBA, PFPeA and PFHxA exhibited complete breakthrough…”), supporting its inclusion in the PFAS scope.
PFPeA is explicitly listed among PFAS in the column results, supporting its inclusion.
PFHxA is explicitly mentioned in the results section describing column breakthrough, supporting its inclusion.
PFHpA is explicitly mentioned in the results section describing breakthrough behavior, supporting its inclusion.
PFOA is repeatedly referenced (e.g., in breakthrough description and regulatory comparison) supporting its inclusion.
6:2FTS is explicitly mentioned among the PFAS evaluated and in discussion of selectivity, supporting its inclusion.
PFBS is listed in the abstract as one of the PFAS whose effluent concentrations were below 10 ng/L, supporting its inclusion.
PFHxS is listed in the abstract among PFAS treated by the AERs, supporting its inclusion.
PFOS is listed in the abstract and in selectivity trend descriptions, supporting its inclusion.
PFNA is listed in the abstract as a PFAS whose effluent concentration was kept below 10 ng/L, supporting its inclusion.
GenX is mentioned in the abstract and discussed in detail as an alternative with relatively poor selectivity except for Gel(12-1-1), supporting its inclusion.
The influent concentration is given as “200 ng/L each” for 11 PFAS in tap water; this matches the value 200.
Concentrations are explicitly reported in ng/L, matching the unit.
EBCT is reported as “3 min,” matching the numeric value 3.
EBCT is in minutes; the unit min matches the text.
The columns were operated with “2000 BV,” matching the value 2000 for bed volumes treated.
Bed volumes are expressed as BV in the article; unit BV is appropriate.

The methods text shows “188.9) << K PFAS/Cl− (median = 595.3),” where the preceding number 188.9 corresponds to the median K_SO4/Cl−. The recorded value 188.9 for the sulfate vs chloride selectivity ratio matches this.
Selectivity coefficients are dimensionless ratios; leaving the unit null is appropriate and consistent with the text.
The text explicitly reports “K PFAS/Cl− (median = 595.3),” matching the recorded value 595.3 for PFAS vs chloride selectivity.
As with other selectivity coefficients, K_PFAS/Cl− is dimensionless; null unit is appropriate.

Across the cited sections, only parent PFAS concentrations and selectivity coefficients among PFAS and anions are discussed; there is no indication of transformation products, fluoride release, or mineralization endpoints. It is reasonable and directly consistent with the evidence to infer that removal is by adsorption only and that no byproducts were characterized.

The article describes “AER columns” operated with controlled BV and EBCT using PFAS-spiked tap water in a lab context, which is characteristic of bench-scale column screening experiments; the early-stage removal focus is explicitly mentioned (“3.4. Early-stage removal of low-concentration PFAS by AER columns”).

The methods and discussion describe a series of polystyrene-based AERs synthesized with different long-alkyl-chain amines, possessing strong-base quaternary amine groups, differing gel vs macroporous structures, and used in column tests for PFAS removal from drinking (tap) water. This matches the treatment description.

result.record_usable_rationale: Core elements—source identity, tap-water matrix, PFAS set, AER treatment identity, operating conditions (influent concentration, EBCT, BV), endpoints (removal and selectivity), and quantitative metrics—are all directly supported by the cited text and correctly transcribed. The only minor issue is an overextended description of AER structures including commercial resins in one operating_conditions field, which does not affect interpretation of core quantitative findings or comparability. The record is therefore usable for synthesis with attention to the noted qualifier issue.
